requiredFindings.title: SetupAbandoned still releases root custody without a successful reap
requiredFindings.finding: The new fail-closed lifetime rule is implemented only once a Child has been constructed. After successful posix_spawn, exit_source can fail and kill_and_reap can return an error; this is the explicitly represented SetupAbandoned branch. That return drops the local ChildScratch, and root_guard has not yet been cloned. If the caller then drops ScratchRoot, no owner retains the invocation lock even though the reap result is uncertain. A sibling sweep can reclaim that root. Drop deliberately leaks its guard for the equivalent uncertain-reap outcome, so the two cleanup paths now implement different custody guarantees. This is a source-analysis finding in the represented cleanup-error branch; no real syscall failure was induced during this constrained review.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Establish root custody for every successfully spawned process before exit-source setup, and preserve or deliberately leak that hold when setup cleanup cannot establish a reap/no-child result. Keep both errors in SetupAbandoned. A small shared guard can serve both the setup-error and Child::drop paths. Add an injected non-EINTR/non-ECHILD reap-error control for the setup-failure branch: after the error and dropping ScratchRoot, the lock must remain held and the root must not be swept. Verify the successful cleanup path still releases its hold.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Deterministic contested-sweep coverage remains outstanding
nonBlockingObservations.observation: Carries D1A-R2-NBO-2. The current two-sweeper/creator stress test may run without forcing both sweepers to retain the same dead root and lock before one wins. Its regression value and the source protocol argument remain valid; a barrier or narrow hook would strengthen interleaving coverage. SCOPE correctly states this was not completed in r3.
